tests: The absolute ceiling: Opus pricing plus 1.35x tokenizer inflation, huge multi-turn input (~12 tool results per call), low cache, and ~2000 calls/day to expose the top of the cost distribution.

expected_truth.how_computed: Model claude-opus-4-7: input $5.00/MTok = 5e-6/tok, output $25.00/MTok = 25e-6/tok, cache_discount 0.90, tokenizer_inflation 1.35. Token counts already include inflation: raw 42000 in * 1.35 = 56700 in_tok; raw 900 out * 1.35 = 1215 out_tok (long multi-turn loop carrying ~12 tool results @ ~3000 tok each + 800 system + tool overhead). cache_frac=0.20, retry_frac=0.05. llm_per_call = (56700*5e-6 + 1215*25e-6) * (1 - 0.20*0.90) * (1 + 0.05) = (0.28350 + 0.030375) * 0.82 * 1.05 = 0.313875 * 0.861 = 0.27025 ~ $0.2702. tool_per_call = 0.15*0.020 + 0.10*0 + 0.10*0 + 0.15*0 + 0.10*0 + 0.15*0 + 0.10*0 + 0.15*0.029 = 0.003 + 0.00435 = 0.00735 (aws.create_snapshot $0.020, stripe.create_charge $0.029; all other actions $0). monthly = 2000 * 30 * (0.2702 + 0.00735 + 0.001) = 60000 * 0.27855 = $16715.78. range = point * [0.85, 1.15] = [14208.42, 19223.15].

why_low_tier_will_miss: The LOW tier assumes 100 calls/day (vs 2000), a small static token estimate (vs 56700 inflated input tokens), and applies no Opus 1.35x tokenizer inflation, so it will under-forecast by ~20-40x; convergence is reached only once live ingestion learns the true call volume, the ~12-tool-result input size, and the Opus inflation multiplier.
